To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the export spillovers of OECD-based multinational enterprises (MNEs) are positive, while the spillovers of overseas Chinese MNEs are insignificant.

(1) Multinational exports increase the probability of local firms exporting, (2) the positive spillovers are driven by OECD-based multinationals, (3) the positive spill overs are more pronounced under the processing trade.
foreign export spillovers are heterogeneous and depend on the type of multinational firms and the type of ownership of the local exporting firms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how foreign export spillovers affect the export behavior of local firms.
the export activity of multinational firms and the impact of such activity on local firms.
the impact of the presence of foreign multinational firms on the export performance of domestic firms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the export activity associated with overseas Chinese firms has no effect on local firms’ exporting decisions, whereas that of multinational firms from OECD countries has a positive influence on the probability of local firms becoming exporters.
foreign exports have a positive impact on the entry decision of local firms in the case of OECD-based multinational firms.
the export activities of overseas Chinese companies have little impact on the probability of export by local firms, while those of OECD-based multinational firms have a positive effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the export spillovers of OECD-based multinational firms are more significant in the Chinese economy.
foreign exports of OECD-based multinational firms have the most positive spillovers for local firms in China.
foreign export spillovers to local firms exist in China, but they are not equally distributed among different types of foreign investors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the export activity associated with overseas Chinese companies does not generate positive export spillovers to local Chinese firms, whereas export activity associated with OECD-based multinational firms does.
the export spillovers of multinational firms are not homogenous across different types of ownership.
the export spillover from foreign-invested firms is heterogeneous.
